title: Publish the Homebrew tap for `battlestar`
description:
## What to build

A tap repository `AvogadroSG1/homebrew-battlestar` carries a `battlestar` formula that downloads the release binary for the machine's architecture and declares `depends_on "beads"`. Needs a human to create the tap repository and grant release permissions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a Mac without Beads, when the user runs `brew install AvogadroSG1/battlestar/battlestar`, then `battlestar` and `bd` are both on PATH.
- [ ] Given a newer release exists, when the user runs `brew upgrade battlestar`, then the new version is installed.
- [ ] Given the formula, when `brew audit` runs, then it passes.

## Blocked by

- Build `battlestar` release binaries in CI

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- None beyond the repository rules in AGENTS.md.
notes: Repo side done: scripts/battlestar-homebrew-formula.mjs (+test) renders Formula/battlestar.rb (on_arm/on_intel URLs+sha256, depends_on beads, herdr-aware launcher); release workflow attaches battlestar.rb. Remaining (human): create AvogadroSG1/homebrew-battlestar, copy battlestar.rb into Formula/, verify brew install/upgrade/audit.

title: Build `battlestar` release binaries in CI
description:
## What to build

Pushing a release tag shaped like `v1.4.0-bs.1` builds `battlestar` binaries for arm64 and x86_64 macOS in GitHub Actions and attaches them, with checksums, to a GitHub release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a pushed release tag, when the workflow finishes, then the GitHub release has both macOS binaries and their checksums.
- [ ] Given a downloaded binary, when `battlestar --version` runs, then it prints the tag's version.
- [ ] Given a tag whose version differs from the package version, when the workflow runs, then it fails before publishing anything.

## Blocked by

- Run the harness as `battlestar` with its own config, upgrades, and version

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- None beyond the repository rules in AGENTS.md.
notes: Repo side done: scripts/battlestar-release-version.mjs (+test), .github/workflows/battlestar-release.yml (verify -> macOS arm64/x64 build + --version smoke -> release with checksums.txt and battlestar.rb), build-binaries.sh emits battlestar-<platform>, upstream workflows skip v*-bs.* tags. Not verified end to end: no release tag pushed yet (user paused before publishing). Close after pushing v1.4.0-bs.1 and confirming the release.

title: Register herdr against the harness on first run
description:
## What to build

On first run, beside the auth and settings copy, the harness registers herdr's pi integration against its own global config. herdr's pi integration honors `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`, so the harness runs herdr's own pi integration install pointed at the harness directory. git-ai is out of scope: its pi hook path is fixed to `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, so the harness does not register, mirror, or copy git-ai, and records no AI authorship until git-ai supports a config-dir override. A missing herdr is skipped silently; an install failure warns and never blocks startup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given herdr is on PATH, when `battlestar` starts the first time, then herdr's pi integration exists in the harness's global extensions and later starts do not reinstall it.
- [ ] Given a herdr pane running `battlestar`, when the agent works and goes idle, then herdr reports those states for the pane.
- [ ] Given git-ai's pi extension exists under `~/.pi/agent/extensions`, when `battlestar` starts, then no git-ai extension is loaded or copied into the harness's global extensions.
- [ ] Given herdr is not installed, when `battlestar` starts, then nothing is registered and no warning appears.
- [ ] Given herdr's install fails, when `battlestar` starts, then a warning names the manual command and startup continues.

## Blocked by

- Run the harness as `battlestar` with its own config, upgrades, and version

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- tdd
- herdr
notes: git-ai dropped from the harness (user decision). Evidence: the git-ai binary builds its pi hook path from the literals .pi/agent/extensions and references no PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR, so git-ai install-hooks cannot target ~/.battlestar/agent. Revisit if git-ai adds a config-dir override.
close_reason: First-run herdr pi integration install; inside herdr the process title is pi so herdr detects the harness. Live smoke: herdr reported working then idle for a battlestar pane.

title: Initialize Beads at publish and honor the Beads opt-out
description:
## What to build

When plan mode publishes in a git repo where `bd` exists but no Beads database does, it asks once. Accepting initializes Beads at the git root and publishes there. Declining records a Beads opt-out in global harness config against the resolved git-root path, publishes to the Markdown tracker, and never asks again for that repo. An existing Beads database always wins. Sequenced after the proposal ticket because both change plan mode's wiring; blocked by the identity ticket so opt-outs land in the harness's own global config.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given a git repo with no Beads database, when the user accepts the prompt, then `bd init --non-interactive --init-if-missing` runs at the git root and the tickets land in Beads.
- [ ] Given the user declines, when publishing finishes, then the opt-out is recorded against the resolved git-root path, the tickets are in the Markdown tracker, and the next publish in that repo does not ask.
- [ ] Given a recorded opt-out, when the user later runs `bd init` and publishes, then Beads is used.
- [ ] Given the working directory is not inside a git repo, when publishing, then there is no prompt and the Markdown tracker is used.
- [ ] Given `bd` is not on PATH, when publishing, then the Markdown tracker is used and the notice names the install command.

## Blocked by

- Always-on plan-mode note and the plan-mode proposal
- Run the harness as `battlestar` with its own config, upgrades, and version

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- tdd
- beads


## Required Skills
tdd,beads
close_reason: Tracker choice at publish: existing Beads DB wins; no DB -> ask once, accept runs bd init --non-interactive --init-if-missing at git root, decline records opt-out in ~/.battlestar/agent/beads-opt-out.json; no git / no bd -> Markdown with brew install beads notice. Red test green; real-bd smoke verified accept/decline/no-git.

title: Always-on plan-mode note and the plan-mode proposal
description:
## What to build

Every interactive session's system prompt carries a short, fixed note that plan mode exists and what it is for. The agent can make a plan-mode proposal; plan mode starts only when the user accepts. Non-interactive runs carry neither. Sequenced after the core-skills ticket because both change plan mode's prompt wiring.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given an interactive session, when the system prompt is built on several turns, then it contains the plan-mode note and the note is byte-identical across turns.
- [ ] Given the agent makes a plan-mode proposal, when the user accepts, then plan mode starts with the request carried over; when the user declines, then nothing changes.
- [ ] Given a print-mode or RPC run, when the session starts, then neither the note nor the proposal tool is present.
- [ ] Given the fresh session after `/plan-execute`, when it starts, then it is in normal mode with write tools.

## Blocked by

- Ship core skills as plan mode's private resources

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- tdd


## Required Skills
tdd
close_reason: Fixed plan_mode system prompt note in tui sessions; propose_plan_mode tool (tui only, confirm to start with request carried over, decline changes nothing); --plan honored only at startup so the /plan-execute session is normal mode. Red tests green.

title: Ship core skills as plan mode's private resources
description:
## What to build

A pinned copy of the ten core skills ships inside the harness and is read only by plan mode, which injects each skill's text into the agent's context in the phase that needs it (ADR 0002). The skills are never registered as pi skills. An explicit sync script refreshes the pinned copy from apm's `.agents/skills/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given an ordinary session, when the system prompt is built, then no core skill name or description appears in it.
- [ ] Given no normal install of tdd, when the user runs `/skill:tdd`, then nothing runs.
- [ ] Given plan mode enters grilling, when the agent's next prompt is built, then the grill-with-docs, grilling, and domain-modeling text is in context; ticketing carries to-tickets; handoff carries handoff; orchestration carries tdd, code-review, diagnosing-bugs, codebase-design, and beads.
- [ ] Given the user installed a different tdd skill normally, when plan mode injects tdd, then the bundled text is used.
- [ ] Given apm updated `.agents/skills/`, when the sync script runs, then the pinned copy matches those ten skills exactly, and before it runs nothing changes.

## Blocked by

- Make plan mode a built-in harness extension and restore upstream's example

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- tdd
- codebase-design


## Required Skills
tdd,codebase-design
close_reason: Pinned core-skills/ copy (10 skills) read only by plan mode; injected per phase (grilling/ticketing/ready/orchestration); no /skill: references; /plan-execute no longer needs a registered /handoff; scripts/sync-core-skills.mjs + npm run sync:core-skills. Red tests green.

title: Run the harness as `battlestar` with its own config, upgrades, and version
description:
## What to build

The harness runs as the `battlestar` command, reads global config from `~/.battlestar/agent` and project config from `.battlestar/` only, and copies `auth.json` and `settings.json` from `~/.pi/agent` once on first run (ADR 0001). It owns its upgrades: `battlestar update self` points at Homebrew, upstream update notices are off, and versions read as the upstream base plus a `bs.N` counter.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given `~/.pi/agent` holds auth, settings, sessions, and extensions and `~/.battlestar/agent` does not exist, when `battlestar` starts the first time, then auth and settings are copied, sessions and extensions are not, and later starts copy nothing.
- [ ] Given a repo with `.pi/extensions/` and `.pi/settings.json`, when `battlestar` runs there, then none of it is loaded.
- [ ] Given `BATTLESTAR_CODING_AGENT_DIR` is set, when `battlestar` starts, then that directory is the global config.
- [ ] Given any install, when the user runs `battlestar update self`, then it prints `brew upgrade battlestar`, changes nothing, and never contacts the upstream npm package.
- [ ] Given upstream publishes a newer pi, when an interactive session starts, then no update notice appears.
- [ ] Given `battlestar --version`, when it runs, then it prints a version shaped like `1.4.0-bs.1`.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- tdd
- codebase-design


## Required Skills
tdd,codebase-design
close_reason: battlestar identity: piConfig name/configDir/harnessRevision, bin battlestar, first-run copy of auth/settings, BATTLESTAR_CODING_AGENT_DIR, update self -> brew upgrade battlestar, upstream notices off, --version 1.4.0-bs.1. Red test test/battlestar-identity.test.ts green; identity fallout tests updated.

title: Make plan mode a built-in harness extension and restore upstream's example
description:
## What to build

Plan mode moves out of the extension examples and ships as one of the harness's built-in extensions, registered beside codemode, mcp, and tool-search. Upstream's plan-mode example is restored exactly as upstream ships it, so upstream merges touch only the built-in registry entry. The existing plan-mode BDD suites move with it and stay green.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given no user or project extensions are installed, when the user runs `/plan`, then plan mode starts and presents the first planning step.
- [ ] Given the restored upstream plan-mode example, when its upstream tests run, then they pass unchanged and the example matches upstream.
- [ ] Given the upstream example is not installed, when the harness starts, then it does not load and only the built-in registers `/plan`.
- [ ] Given the user also installs the upstream example, when the harness starts, then the duplicate `/plan` is reported and the built-in plan mode stays active.
- [ ] Given the user disables the built-in in settings (like `-builtin:mcp`), when the harness starts, then `/plan` is absent.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately).

## Required skills

Load each skill before starting with `/skill:<name>`.

- codebase-design
- tdd


## Required Skills
codebase-design,tdd
close_reason: Built-in plan-mode extension registered as builtin:plan-mode; upstream example and tests restored byte-identical to d5b3de22d; duplicate /plan reported and built-in keeps bare name; suites moved to test/builtin-plan-mode-*; red test test/suite/builtin-plan-mode.test.ts green.

title: Battlestar harness: plan mode as the built-in default
description:
## Outcome

battlestar-pi becomes the user's opinionated harness: installed globally as `battlestar`, with plan mode built in, its core skills private to plan mode, and Beads as the default tracker with a Markdown fallback.

## Scope

Built-in plan mode, separate harness identity and upgrades, private core skills, always-on plan-mode note and plan-mode proposal, Beads init at publish with the Beads opt-out, first-run herdr integration registration, CI release binaries, and a Homebrew tap.

Vocabulary: GLOSSARY.md (Harness, Plan mode, Plan-mode proposal, Core skills, Tracker, Markdown tracker, Beads opt-out).
Decisions: docs/adr/0001-separate-harness-identity.md, docs/adr/0002-core-skills-private-to-plan-mode.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fresh `battlestar` install has `/plan` with no extension installed, in every repo.
- [ ] The harness runs as `battlestar` with its own global and project config, separate from stock pi, and owns its upgrades.
- [ ] Core skills never cost context outside plan mode and are injected per plan-mode phase from a pinned copy.
- [ ] Interactive sessions carry the plan-mode note and the plan-mode proposal; non-interactive runs carry neither.
- [ ] Publishing initializes Beads on consent, records a Beads opt-out on refusal, and otherwise falls back to the Markdown tracker.
- [ ] `brew install` of the tap installs the harness and Beads; first run registers herdr against the harness.
notes: When completed and verified, commit and push into main.

title: Draft, review, and publish dependency-aware tickets
description:
## What to build
The agent and user collaboratively draft, review, and publish dependency-aware implementation tickets under a Beads epic. Every ticket carries a BDD contract and relevant repository-skill guidance for its implementor.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given the mental models are confirmed, when tickets are drafted, then they are tracer-bullet slices with explicit dependency information.
- [ ] Given any ticket is drafted, then it includes a user-observable BDD contract and names relevant repository skills with guidance to load them.
- [ ] Given the user is reviewing the ticket set, then the agent asks about granularity and dependency correctness, iterates until the user approves, and only then publishes.
- [ ] Given approved tickets and an initialized Beads database, when publishing, then the agent creates one epic and its child tickets in dependency order.
- [ ] Given ticket blockers exist, when tickets are published, then native Beads dependency edges represent them and the ticket text makes blockers clear.
- [ ] Given Beads is not initialized or usable, when publishing is needed, then the workflow writes Markdown tickets instead of failing or silently dropping the dependency graph.

## Blocked by
Planning readiness, grilling, and shared mental-model confirmation.

## Required skills
- `to-tickets`: vertical slicing, review, dependency modeling, and publication.
- `tdd`: tests for ticket and dependency representations.


## Required Skills
to-tickets,tdd

title: Agree on execution order and hand off to a fresh session
description:
## What to build
Before implementation, the orchestrator reads the tracker to identify ticket order and parallelizable work, agrees on the schedule with the user, then starts a fresh session using `/handoff`, exits plan mode, and invokes `/new`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given published tickets, when preparing execution, then the orchestrator reads statuses and dependency edges to identify ready work, ordering, and safe parallelism.
- [ ] Given an execution schedule is proposed, when the user and orchestrator agree on it, then the schedule and ticket references are included in `/handoff`.
- [ ] Given the user chooses Execute and clear context, when the handoff is ready, then the agent exits plan mode and starts `/new` with the handoff instructions.
- [ ] Given the fresh session starts, then orchestration begins from the approved schedule without asking the user to approve it a second time.
- [ ] Given `/handoff` or `/new` is unavailable, then execution pauses and the user is told what manual action is needed.

## Blocked by
Drafting, reviewing, and publishing the approved dependency-aware ticket set.

## Required skills
- `handoff`: write the fresh-session handoff.
- `to-tickets`: interpret tracker tickets and blockers.
- `codebase-design`: keep the session transition and handoff boundary explicit.


## Required Skills
handoff,to-tickets,codebase-design

title: Delegate implementation, verify tickets, and resolve stuck work
description:
## What to build
In the fresh session, the orchestrator creates a BDD red test before handing a ticket to an implementor, dispatches only tickets whose blockers are complete, parallelizes independent ready tickets, verifies completed work, and closes tickets. It enforces bounded help/review cycles and resolves stuck work through joint framing and arbitration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a ticket is ready, when the orchestrator dispatches it, then the orchestrator first creates/provides the failing BDD test and acceptance contract.
- [ ] Given a ticket has incomplete blockers, then it is not dispatched; given independent tickets are ready, then they may be dispatched in parallel.
- [ ] Given an implementor asks for help, then it may request orchestrator help at most twice during the ticket attempt.
- [ ] Given completed work is returned, then the orchestrator verifies it, sends findings for fixes when needed, and performs at most two ordinary review/fix cycles before escalation.
- [ ] Given ordinary cycles do not resolve the disagreement, then the implementor and orchestrator fill and review `docs/planning_support_docs/joint-framing.md`; agreement on a pathway grants one additional work/review cycle.
- [ ] Given no pathway is agreed, then a medium-reasoning subagent arbitrates using the completed joint framing; for destructive-data or security concerns, work pauses and the arbitrator asks the user what to do and carries that decision through resolution.
- [ ] Given a ticket meets its BDD contract and acceptance criteria, then the orchestrator closes it in Beads (or marks it complete in Markdown) before dispatching newly unblocked work.
- [ ] Given arbitration or a work limit requires human input, then affected work remains paused until the decision is returned.

## Blocked by
Tracker-derived execution order and parallelization agreed, then `/handoff` and `/new` start the fresh session.

## Required skills
- `tdd`: BDD red/green implementation.
- `code-review`: verify completed work and report actionable findings.
- `diagnosing-bugs`: diagnose blocked or failing work.
- `joint-framing.md`: follow the repository's shared-framing and escalation artifact.


## Required Skills
tdd,code-review,diagnosing-bugs

title: Add plan-mode entry, lifecycle, and exit choices
description:
## What to build
A user can start `/plan`, stay in a distinct planning mode while the preparation workflow runs, and explicitly choose either to exit without further action or to proceed to execution after planning is complete.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a user invokes `/plan`, when the workflow starts, then Pi enters plan mode and presents the first planning step.
- [ ] Given plan mode is active, when planning or ticket publication is in progress, then the workflow remains in plan mode.
- [ ] Given the user chooses “Exit Plan Mode,” when the choice is confirmed, then planning ends without publishing additional work or starting implementation.
- [ ] Given the user chooses “Execute and clear context,” when the approved schedule is ready, then plan mode can exit into the fresh-session handoff flow.

## Blocked by
None (can start immediately).

## Required skills
- `tdd`: add behavior tests before implementation.
- `codebase-design`: use when defining the plan-mode state boundary and lifecycle.


## Required Skills
tdd,codebase-design

title: Drive planning through readiness assessment and approved skills
description:
## What to build
The agent transparently recommends whether the request is ready for ticketing or needs requirements discovery. When needed, it uses `grill-with-docs`, confirms the user's desired-outcome and system/domain mental models, and returns to grilling if ticket drafting exposes unresolved requirements.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Given a request, when readiness is assessed, then the agent explains its recommendation to grill first or go directly to ticketing and lets the user choose if they disagree.
- [ ] Given grilling is needed, when requirements are explored, then the workflow invokes `grill-with-docs` (which uses `grilling` and `domain-modeling`) rather than a separate plan-generation mode.
- [ ] Given grilling is complete, when ticketing is about to start, then the user and agent explicitly confirm both the desired outcome/constraints and relevant system/domain understanding.
- [ ] Given ticket drafting reveals an undecided requirement, when the gap is found, then the workflow returns to grilling and affected tickets are reviewed again before publication.

## Blocked by
Plan mode lifecycle and exit choices.

## Required skills
- `grill-with-docs`: requirements discovery and documentation workflow.
- `grilling`: readiness assessment and shared understanding.
- `domain-modeling`: domain terminology and system mental model.
- `to-tickets`: ticket drafting handoff.


## Required Skills
grill-with-docs,grilling,domain-modeling,to-tickets

title: Collaborative skill-driven plan mode and execution orchestration
description:
## Outcome
Add a collaborative plan mode to Pi that uses the repository's `grill-with-docs` and `to-tickets` skills for planning, then hands approved work to an orchestrator in a fresh session.

## Scope
The workflow covers readiness assessment, requirements discovery, shared mental-model confirmation, ticket drafting/review/publication, tracker-derived execution scheduling, `/handoff` + `/new`, dependency-aware implementation delegation, ticket verification/closure, and bounded disagreement escalation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `/plan` remains in plan mode through planning and ticket publication until the user chooses Exit Plan Mode or Execute and clear context.
- [ ] Planning uses the approved skills and returns to grilling when ticketing exposes unresolved requirements.
- [ ] Tickets have BDD contracts and relevant repository-skill guidance, and are published under a Beads epic with dependency edges.
- [ ] The user and orchestrator agree on execution order and parallelization before execution starts.
- [ ] Execute creates a `/handoff`, exits plan mode, starts `/new`, and begins orchestration in the fresh session.
- [ ] Implementation respects blockers, BDD red/green, bounded help/review cycles, and ticket closure.
- [ ] Unresolved disagreement uses `docs/planning_support_docs/joint-framing.md` and medium-reasoning subagent arbitration; destructive-data or security concerns pause for the user's direction through the arbitrator.

## Work breakdown
See child issues for the dependency-ordered implementation slices.
